title: Noise and Averaging Bench
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Discover the square-root rule yourself, verify it against the measurement, then meet the two costs that make "average more" the wrong answer.

learningObjectives: Justify a choice of averaging depth for a given sensor and purpose.
Weigh noise reduction against power cost and against the risk of smoothing away a real event.
prerequisites: The Accuracy Versus Precision MicroSim from Chapter 2
Knowing what a standard deviation describes

keyQuestions: Averaging 256 readings instead of 64 cuts the noise by half. What does it cost?
Why does averaging cost almost nothing in Slow change mode?
Your station is for catching sudden events. Does that argue for more averaging or less?
commonMisconceptions: Believing more averaging is always better.
Expecting the noise to fall in proportion to N rather than to the square root of N.
Assuming a smoother line is a more accurate line.
assessmentOpportunities: Justifies a specific averaging depth by reference to more than one cost.
Explains the square-root rule and can say what it does not promise.
Recognises that a filter which removes noise also removes fast real signals.
